    AI Overview
    Yes, Cameron and Cayden Boozer are fraternal twins. Born in 2007 to former NBA player Carlos Boozer and CeCe Boozer, they are high-profile basketball recruits who committed to play for the Duke Blue Devils. The twins were born to be a genetic match to cure their older brother's sickle cell disease. 
    This video tells the story of how Cameron and Cayden Boozer were born to help their older brother:
    00:59
    Front Office Sports
    YouTube• Mar 21, 2026
    Key details about the Boozer twins: 
    • Background: They were born in Salt Lake City on July 18, 2007, and grew up in Florida.
    • Basketball Careers: Both are top-tier recruits. Cameron is a 6'9" forward, and Cayden is a 6'5" point guard.
    • Family: They are the sons of former NBA All-Star Carlos Boozer and CeCe Boozer.
    • Sibling Connection: The twins were conceived via IVF to provide a bone marrow match for their older brother, Carmani, who was diagnosed with sickle cell disease, according to the Front Office Sports Instagram post. 
    They announced their commitment to play for Duke in 2026, continuing their father's legacy at the school.

    Cameron and Cayden Boozer, the Duke basketball freshmen and sons of former NBA player Carlos Boozer, are fraternal twins. Born on July 18, 2007, they are not identical and have different physical builds; Cameron is a 6-foot-9 forward, while Cayden is a 6-foot-3 point guard. 
    • Birth Story: The twins were conceived via IVF to be a stem cell match for their older brother, Carmani, who was diagnosed with sickle cell disease.
    • Physical Differences: They are easily distinguished by their size, with nearly a five-inch and 50-pound difference, according to USA Today.
    • Basketball Career: Both are top-tier recruits playing for Duke University as of the 2025-2026 season, say
